{{technical|date=July 2025}}
[[Image:Agilent-pna-x-advanced-design-system.jpg|thumb| Agilent engineer demonstrates X-parameter functionality at [[IEEE]] [[IEEE Microwave Theory and Techniques Society|MTT-S]] [[IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Symposium|International Microwave Symposium]], Boston MA June 10, 2009.)]]
'''X-parameters''' are a generalization of [[Scattering parameters|S-parameters]] and are used for characterizing the amplitudes and relative phase of harmonics generated by nonlinear components under large input power levels.  X-parameters are also referred to as the parameters of the Poly-Harmonic Distortion (PHD) nonlinear behavioral model.

==Description==
'''X-parameters''' represent a new category of [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] [[Network analysis (electrical circuits)|network parameters]] for high-frequency design (Nonlinear vector network analyzers are sometimes called large signal network analyzers.<ref>{{cite journal
| author = Dr. Jan Verspecht
|date=December 2005
| title       = Large-Signal Network Analysis
| journal     = IEEE Microwave Magazine
| volume      = 6
| issue       = 4
| pages       = 82–92
| publisher   = IEEE
| url         = http://www.janverspecht.com/pdf/lsnaieeemicrowavemagazine.pdf
| access-date  = May 1, 2009
| doi = 10.1109/MMW.2005.1580340
|bibcode=2005IMMag...6d..82V
|s2cid=23109051
}}
</ref>)

X-parameters are applicable to both [[Large-signal model|large-signal]] and [[Small-signal model|small-signal]] conditions, for linear and nonlinear components.  They are an extension of [[Scattering parameters|S-parameters]]<ref>{{cite journal
| url = http://www.mwjournal.com/article.asp?HH_ID=AR_7439
| title = EDA Focus: May 2009, Transcript of interview of David E. Root by Microwave Journal Editor David Vye on April 16th, 2009.
| journal = Microwave Journal
| date = April 16, 2009
| access-date = May 4, 2009
| archive-date = July 14, 2011
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110714142543/http://www.mwjournal.com/article.asp?HH_ID=AR_7439
| url-status = dead
}}</ref> meaning that, in the limit of a small signal, X-parameters reduce to S-parameters.

They help overcome a key challenge in [[RF engineering]], namely that nonlinear [[Electrical impedance|impedance]] differences, [[Frequency mixer|harmonic mixing]], and nonlinear reflection effects occur when components are cascaded under large signal operating conditions. This means that there is a nonlinear and as such non-trivial relationship between the properties of the individual cascaded components and the composite properties of the resulting cascade. This situation is unlike that at [[Direct current|DC]], where one can simply add the values of [[resistor]]s connected in series. X-parameters help solve this cascading problem: if the X-parameters of a set of components are measured individually, the X-parameters (and hence the non-linear transfer function) can be calculated of any cascade made from them. Calculations based on X-parameters are usually performed within a harmonic balance simulator environment.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.keysight.com/main/editorial.jspx?cc=US&lc=eng&ckey=1619575&nid=-33038.775208.02&id=1619575
| title = Keysight NVNA & X-Parameters Simulation in ADS: The new paradigm for nonlinear measurements, modeling, and simulation with ADS (PDF, 1MB) on the X-Parameters MMIC Design Seminar page
|access-date = July 17, 2015
}}</ref>

==Development ==
X-parameters were developed and introduced by [[Keysight Technologies]] as functionality included in [https://www.keysight.com/us/en/product/N5242A/pnax-microwave-network-analyzer-265-ghz.html N5242A Nonlinear Vector Network Analyzer],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://about.keysight.com/en/newsroom/imagelibrary/2008/17dec-em08200/|title=Agilent Technologies Announces Breakthrough in X-Parameter Nonlinear Model Generation for Components Used in Wireless, Aerospace Defense Industries: X-Parameters Enable Model Generation from Simulation or Measurement, for Fast Development|date=December 17, 2008|website=Keysight.com|access-date=May 6, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.keysight.com/find/nvna
|title=Keysight N5242A PNA-X Series Microwave Network Analyzer, 10 MHz to 26.5 GHz
|access-date=July 17, 2015
}}</ref>  and the W2200 [[Advanced Design System]] in 2008.

X-parameters are the parameters of the polyharmonic distortion modeling work of Dr. Jan Verspecht<ref>{{cite journal
| url = http://users.skynet.be/jan.verspecht/Work/BlackBoxPowerTransistorsINMMC96.pdf
| title = Black Box Modelling of Power Transistors in the Frequency Domain
| author = Dr. Jan Verspecht
| journal = Conference Paper Presented at the INMMC '96, Duisburg, Germany
| date = October 1996
| access-date = May 6, 2009
| archive-date = December 14, 2010
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101214164246/http://users.skynet.be/jan.verspecht/Work/BlackBoxPowerTransistorsINMMC96.pdf
| url-status = dead
}} (PDF, 85 KB)</ref><ref name=vr>{{cite journal
| url = http://www.janverspecht.com/pdf/phd_ieeemicrowavemagazine.pdf
| title = Polyharmonic Distortion Modeling
| author = Dr. Jan Verspecht
|author2=Dr. David E. Root 
| journal = IEEE Microwave Magazine
| volume = 7
| issue = 3
|date=June 2006
| pages = 44–57
| publisher   = IEEE
| access-date=May 6, 2009
| doi = 10.1109/MMW.2006.1638289
| bibcode = 2006IMMag...7c..44V
| s2cid = 20488542
}} (PDF, 2.4MB)</ref>  and Dr. David E. Root.<ref name=vr/>
